question: Why does google/embeddinggemma-2 use different prompt prefixes for queries ('task: search result | query: ...') and documents ('title: ... | text: ...')?
options: To make the strings longer so they use more RAM
Because question-to-passage retrieval is asymmetric: short questions and long factual passages have different syntactic structures that must be mapped into aligned locations on the unit hypersphere
Because Python strings require a pipe character
explanation: Asymmetric task prefixes instruct the encoder to project short interrogative queries and long declarative documents into mutually aligned coordinates.

question: What happens if you compute last_hidden_state.mean(dim=1) on a padded batch without multiplying by the attention mask?
options: Padding tokens ([PAD]) are averaged into the embedding, causing a short sentence's vector to change depending on the max sequence length of the batch
Nothing changes because [PAD] tokens always have hidden state 0
explanation: Transformer layers apply bias terms and LayerNorm to every position, so [PAD] positions have non-zero hidden states that corrupt unmasked averages.

question: In the masked mean pooling equation p = (sum_t m_t * h_t) / sum_t m_t, what does the denominator sum_t m_t represent?
options: The exact number of non-padding (real) tokens in that specific sequence
explanation: Since m_t is 1 for real tokens and 0 for padding, sum_t m_t counts the true sequence length of each item in the batch.

question: Why do we prepend 'title: {title} | text: {content}' to every chunk in src/chunker.py?
options: So chunks that use pronouns or relative references ('This endpoint accepts...') retain their parent document and section context inside the dense vector
Because BM25 only indexes the word 'title'
explanation: Injecting the document and section title into the embedding prompt disambiguates chunks whose body text alone lacks the product or endpoint name.
